title: Volumetric Light
description: Volumetric lighting makes beams visible through haze, fog, dust, smoke, or other particles, so the air photographs as well as the subject. Also called god rays or crepuscular rays when the shafts are distinct.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Air has to be photographed. A cathedral, a forest, a smoky archive: the beam is architecture.
The source implies a world outside the frame. Without particles you only see where the light lands, not the path it took.
It is the wrong tool in clean air if you still want shafts, or when haze is so thick that every depth plane flattens. Disconnected glowing stripes with no lamp are not volumetric light.
They are stickers.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: You need a directional source (often hard, slightly back or high) and a scattering medium: haze, dust, rain, smoke. The camera usually sees some of the beam angle, which is why backlight helps.
Color follows the source: warm sun, cool window, searchlight white. Limit haze so foreground and background still separate.
Prompt: Volumetric rays through haze around [Subject], visible beams, dust in the shaft, cathedral or forest light as architecture.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when the air is part of the picture, a smoky interior, a forest morning, a searchlight. Do not add floating stripes with no source and no medium.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a backlight rim with no air, or painted god-ray stickers. The tell is stripes that ignore the lamp and the body.
Fix it by adding a scattering medium and a real rear or high source, then letting the body interrupt the beam.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is volumetric light in film?
Beams made visible by haze, fog, dust, smoke, or particles. You photograph the path of the light, not only where it lands.
Volumetric light vs backlight
Backlight is the direction from behind. Volumetric light is the beam made visible in a medium. Backlight often helps you see that beam.
When should I use volumetric light?
Use it when air, dust, or smoke should be visible architecture. Skip it in clean air, or when haze would flatten every plane.
How do I prompt volumetric light for AI image or video?
Specify a real source and a scattering medium, visible beams, dust in the shaft. The body can interrupt the beam. No orphan glowing stripes.
